title: A proximity‑based multi‑indicator framework for optimizing emergency shelter layout in a mountainous city: A case study of Dujiangyan, China
content:
by Gang Chen, Yanxi Chen, Jiangyue Fu, Yi Yang, Xinchuan Liu

Emergency shelters play a vital role in protecting human life in disaster‑prone regions such as China. However, in many high‑risk cities, existing emergency shelter systems are often planned for single hazards and exhibit spatial layouts that are poorly aligned with population distribution, thereby undermining evacuation efficiency and post‑disaster resettlement capacity. To address these limitations, this study proposes a GIS‑based proximity‑driven framework for hazard exposure assessment and spatial optimization of emergency shelters, with Dujiangyan City, China, as a case study. First, a hazard exposure evaluation system was constructed using proximity‑to‑source indicators for major threats, including earthquakes, geological hazards (e.g., landslides and debris flows), floods, and secondary fires. Second, an integrated weighting approach combining the Entropy Weight Method (EWM) and Random Forest (RF) was developed to quantitatively assess the suitability of both existing and candidate shelter sites across the four hazard types. Third, a multi‑objective spatial optimization model was designed to simultaneously balance shelter site quality and the structural performance of the shelter network, enabling the selection of an optimized shelter configuration. Compared with the existing configuration of 135 shelters, the optimized scheme maintains the same shelter count, enabling a direct comparison that isolates the effect of spatial reconfiguration. Population coverage improves from 55.9% to 66.1%, expanding the covered population from 393,927–465,732 people. Per‑shelter service efficiency moderately increases from 2,918–3,450 people per shelter. The overlap rate substantially decreases from 87.6% to 56.8%, reflecting reduced service redundancy. The average safety score shows a modest decline from 0.4577 to 0.4409, an acceptable trade-off given the substantial gains in coverage and efficiency. This study provides a data‑driven decision‑support tool for enhancing urban disaster preparedness and resilience in Dujiangyan City and offers a transferable methodological framework for emergency shelter planning in other cities facing complex hazard risks.
